evidence.text: Topics. algorithms and auction dynamics / Deconstructing Meta's Andromeda algorithm and the shift to vector-based targeting, where the ad creative itself dictates audience selection, replacing deprecated interest/lookalike targeting. Explaining the "Creative Similarity Score" and how Andromeda bundles visually or thematically similar creatives under a single entity ID; this restricts unique reach, forces ads to compete for the same cluster, and artificially drives up frequency while degrading Return on Ad Spend (ROAS). Managing ad sequencing within the algorithm, recognizing that Meta optimizes for multi-click and view-through journeys, making ad-level last-click ROAS highly unreliable for top-of-funnel creative. campaign setup and tracking / Architecting ad accounts to support algorithmic learning by consolidating creative variations into concept-specific adsets (Persona + Angle + Offer). Avoiding the common error of segmenting adsets by arbitrary traits (e.g., launch dates) or mixing conflicting personas (e.g., men and women) within the same adset, which confuses the machine learning targeting models. Managing the risk of Dynamic Product Ads (DPAs) causing a "death spiral" by masking poor top-of-funnel performance with inflated bottom-of-funnel retargeting ROAS. scaling / Implementing a portfolio management approach to ad scaling to avoid the risk of relying on a single "hero ad" that inevitably reaches its maximum daily spend capacity and fatigues. Utilizing Campaign Budget Optimization (CBO) to leverage Pareto’s Principle (where 4% of ads command 64% of spend) for maximum efficiency, while carefully monitoring to prevent over-concentration that exposes the business to sudden revenue drops. Recommending a minimum allocation of 10% to 25% of the total media budget directly toward creative production to maintain the volume required to combat ad fatigue.

cards.title: Creative Similarity Score clustering and unique reach limits
cards.claim: Meta's Andromeda algorithm bundles visually or thematically similar creatives under a single entity ID via a "Creative Similarity Score"; this restricts unique reach, forces ads to compete for the same cluster, artificially drives up frequency while degrading Return on Ad Spend (ROAS).
cards.action: Track Creative Similarity Score clustering and unique reach, and produce visually/thematically differentiated creatives to avoid being bundled under one entity ID.
applies_when: Running multiple creatives under Meta's Andromeda algorithm
Creatives are visually or thematically similar
do_not_use_when: The passage does not describe a scenario for not using this observation
unknowns: The threshold values used in the Creative Similarity Score
How much unique reach is lost per cluster
evidence_quotes: Deconstructing Meta's Andromeda algorithm and the shift to vector-based targeting, where the ad creative itself dictates audience selection, replacing deprecated interest/lookalike targeting

Explaining the "Creative Similarity Score" and how Andromeda bundles visually or thematically similar creatives under a single entity ID; this restricts unique reach, forces ads to compete for the same cluster, and artificially drives up frequency while degrading Return on Ad Spend (ROAS).

cards.title: Adset structure for algorithmic learning
cards.claim: Ad accounts should be architected to support algorithmic learning by consolidating creative variations into concept-specific adsets (Persona + Angle + Offer); segmenting adsets by arbitrary traits such as launch dates or mixing conflicting personas such as men and women within the same adset confuses the machine learning targeting models.
cards.action: Consolidate creative variations into concept-specific adsets based on Persona + Angle + Offer; avoid segmenting adsets by arbitrary traits like launch dates and avoid mixing conflicting personas within one adset.
applies_when: Setting up ad accounts for algorithmic learning
do_not_use_when: The passage does not describe a scenario for not using this observation
unknowns: How many creatives per concept-specific adset is optimal
How the machine learning model reacts numerically when personas are mixed
evidence_quotes: Architecting ad accounts to support algorithmic learning by consolidating creative variations into concept-specific adsets (Persona + Angle + Offer).

Avoiding the common error of segmenting adsets by arbitrary traits (e.g., launch dates) or mixing conflicting personas (e.g., men and women) within the same adset, which confuses the machine learning targeting models.

cards.title: Dynamic Product Ads masking top-of-funnel performance
cards.claim: Dynamic Product Ads (DPAs) can cause a "death spiral" by masking poor top-of-funnel performance with inflated bottom-of-funnel retargeting ROAS.
cards.action: Manage the risk of DPAs masking poor top-of-funnel performance with inflated bottom-of-funnel retargeting ROAS.
applies_when: Using Dynamic Product Ads with bottom-of-funnel retargeting
do_not_use_when: The passage does not describe a scenario for not using this observation
unknowns: The specific metrics or thresholds that indicate DPA masking
How to separate true top-of-funnel performance from retargeting inflation
evidence_quotes: Managing the risk of Dynamic Product Ads (DPAs) causing a "death spiral" by masking poor top-of-funnel performance with inflated bottom-of-funnel retargeting ROAS.
